title: Cootie Williams and the Savoy against Ellington
summary: He recalls Cootie, plunger mutes and the Savoy crowd favoring his band over Duke's.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving

blocks.x: That's good. And other trumpet players besides Roy, like Cootie

Oh yeah. Cootie. Cootie with Duke. He was, he and I was good friends. Cootie was good. He had his style. I didn't know about I never, nobody plungers until I heard Cootie. Dud used to do a lot of plungers after that too. I remember the time when Ivie Anderson was singing with Duke Ellington and they played the Savoy. Cootie, Freddie Jenkins, I think was in his section, I can't think of the other trumpet player. And, we were on this stand and they were on that stand. Ivie Anderson used to kid them all the time and say, 'Them young boys will run you all out of here.' You know, things, just kidding things. And, the Savoy actually went for us more than they did for Duke. Now, we know Duke played all that music all over us, you know. But, they just stood up there and they looked at us and they just started blowing a tune because Duke had been around so long. You know? But Cootie, after the band, we used
to go out and jam. I used to have to drive Cootie home somtimes. We both had had our little fun. We used to hang out together. We were in the Savoy together years ago.
